Nefarious

/nih-FAIR-ee-us/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Nefarious means wicked and villainous in a calculated, scheming way — used for evil plots, schemes, and the people behind them.

In the spy film, the agent races to stop a nefarious plot to blackmail half the city's judges.

Worked Example

Investigators finally untangled the accountant's nefarious scheme, which had quietly siphoned pension money into shell companies for a decade.

The scheme was deliberate, secretive, and sustained over years — exactly the calculated, plotting kind of wickedness nefarious describes, not a one-time lapse or an accident.

How Nefarious Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

villainous

villainous: wicked in the manner of a story's villain

iniquitous

iniquitous: grossly unjust and immoral

Antonyms

virtuous

virtuous: morally good and upright

honorable

honorable: principled and worthy of respect

How Strong Is It? — shady → nefarious → diabolical

shady vs. nefarious

shady vs. nefarious: A shady deal merely cuts ethical corners, but a nefarious scheme is built on deliberate, calculated wrongdoing.

diabolical vs. nefarious

diabolical vs. nefarious: Diabolical goes even further than nefarious, suggesting evil so elaborate it seems almost demonic.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ne-

Prefix — ne-: not (Latin)

Root — far

Root — far: divine law; what is right (Latin fas — its s softens to r inside the Latin adjective nefarius)

Suffix — -ious

Suffix — -ious: characterized by; full of

Put it together

Put it together: Ne- (not) + far (divine law, what is right — Latin fas, whose s softens to r inside the Latin adjective nefarius) + -ious (characterized by, full of): nefarious literally means 'characterized by what is not right' — behavior that breaks the deepest rules of law and morality. The root survives almost nowhere else in English, so treat this as the word's origin story rather than a reusable building block.

Use the root in a new word: negate

Use the root in a new word: negate: The prefix ne- ('not') also appears in negate: one honest witness can negate an entire afternoon of careful lying.

Root Check

Word Choice

Literary / journalistic

Use nefarious for a scheming person, plot, or scheme whose wickedness is deliberate and often secretive — 'a nefarious plot,' 'his nefarious dealings.' Keep it distinct from heinous, which describes one specific act so shockingly evil it provokes outrage: a nefarious mastermind may commit a heinous crime, but the mastermind and the plotting are what nefarious describes.
